source.subject: add searchable map titles and catalog monitoring

answers.question: How do I install QSS-M and where do my Quake files go?
answers.answer:
The install process itself isn't covered here, but the file layout is.

QSS-M expects a base directory containing the engine and all game directories [1]. Your Quake data lives in an `id1` folder under that base directory — the game always searches `id1` there [2], and saves go to `quake/id1/` [3][4]. Backups such as IP logs are stored in `id1/backups/` [5][6].

To see exactly which paths are in use, type `path` in the console; it prints the fully qualified paths, including `.pak` files, which count as path locations [7].

If you want config, saves, and generated files kept in the installation folder instead of a separate user-data directory on Unix/macOS, launch with `-nohome` [8]. To point the engine at a different base directory, use `-basedir` followed by the path, e.g. `-basedir c:\quake` [1].

answers.question: Where are my settings saved, and how do I use an autoexec.cfg?
answers.answer:
Your settings live in `config.cfg`. They autosave when you quit, but a crash means they aren't saved — so after changing things you care about, run `writeconfig` to save on the spot [1]. You can also save to a different file by giving an argument, e.g. `writeconfig mycfg` (a `.cfg` extension is added automatically) [1][2].

To load a config file, use `exec`, e.g. `exec autoexec.cfg`. It runs every line in the file; lines starting with `//` are ignored, and you can use relative paths with `/` or `\` (absolute paths like `c:\quake` won't work) [3]. Files named `autoexec.cfg`, `config.cfg`, `server.cfg`, `connect.cfg`, `ctf.cfg`, `dm.cfg`, and `end.cfg` are treated as config files [4].

You can also have a config run at startup via `cl_onload`, for example `cl_onload "exec autoexec.cfg"`; its default is empty, which shows the main menu [5].

answers.question: How do I run a mod or mission pack?
answers.answer:
Type `game <modname>` in the console to load a mod on the fly — it's the same as `gamedir` [1]. For example, `game mymod` switches to that directory. You can also set it at startup with the `-game` launch option, e.g. `-game mymod` [2].

For the official mission packs, use the launch options `-hipnotic` (Scourge of Armagon), `-rogue` (Dissolution of Eternity), or `-quoth` [3][4][5]. Only one of these should be specified at a time [3].

In cooperative games, a server can enable `sv_modvote 1` (default `0`) so eligible players can use `modvote` to switch to another installed mod by majority vote [6].

Note that `gamecfg` is a general-purpose variable whose meaning depends on the mod, not a mod loader [7].

answers.question: How do I download and play custom maps?
answers.answer:
Use the `download` command, then load the map.

- `download aerowalk.bsp` fetches the map using the web download URLs, which are much faster than downloading from the server [1]. It can also grab `.lit`, `.wav`, and `.loc` files [1].
- The two web sources are `cl_web_download_url`, default `q1tools/q1tools.github.io` [2], and `cl_web_download_url2`, default `maps.quakeworld.nu` [3]. If either is blank, only the connected server is tried [2][3].
- To play it, type `map aerowalk` (or the map's name without `.bsp`) [4]. On a server, `map` disconnects everyone, so `changelevel` is recommended there [4].
- To find maps, `maps` lists all maps with their descriptions; `maps chamber` searches them [5].
- You can also drop additional maps into the `id1/maps/` folder and load them from there [4].

answers.question: How do I reset everything back to the defaults?
answers.answer:
Type `resetall` in the console to reset every console variable to its engine default [1]. That's the broadest option.

If you only want to undo the settings that get saved to your config file, use `resetcfg` instead — it resets only the cvars that archive to the config, leaving the rest alone [2]. Some cvars never save to the config and can only be set in-game or through an autoexec, so `resetcfg` won't touch those [2].

To reset one setting at a time, use `reset <cvar>`, for example `reset cl_backspeed` [3]. Note this restores the engine default, not whatever value was in your default.cfg [3].

After resetting, run `writeconfig` to save the current settings to config.cfg immediately — useful if the game might crash before it autosaves on quit [4].

answers.question: How do I change my field of view?
answers.answer:
Open the console and type `fov 110` (or any value). The default is `90`, and valid values are 10–170 [1]. The setting is saved to your config [1].

- `fov_adapt` defaults to `1` and automatically scales FOV for widescreen resolutions, so widescreen players see more to the sides instead of losing top/bottom view [2]. It is enabled by default [2].
- `cl_gun_fovscale` defaults to `1` and compensates for viewmodel distortion when `fov` is above 90; QSS-M also accepts floats above or below 1 to adjust the amount of distortion, and it is not affected by `fov` [3].

answers.question: How do I change resolution, fullscreen, and vsync?
answers.answer:
Change resolution with `vid_width` and `vid_height`, then run `vid_restart`. Defaults are `vid_width 800` and `vid_height 600` [1][2]. For example: `vid_width 1920`, `vid_height 1080`, `vid_restart`.

Fullscreen: set `vid_fullscreen 1` and run `vid_restart`; default is `0` (windowed) [3][4]. You can also start fullscreen with the `-fullscreen` launch option [5]. For windowed fullscreen, use `vid_desktopfullscreen 1` [6].

Vsync: `vid_vsync 1` enables it, `vid_vsync 0` disables it; default is `0` [7].

In fullscreen, `vid_bpp` defaults to `16` and `vid_refreshrate` to `60` [8][9]. Resolution, fullscreen, bpp, and refreshrate changes need `vid_restart` to take effect [3][2][1][4][8][9]. Manually resized window sizes are saved to `vid_width`/`vid_height` when `vid_saveresize` is `1` (default) [10].

answers.question: How do I uncap or limit my framerate?
answers.answer:
Type `host_maxfps 0` to uncap your framerate. The default is `250` [1]. Note that `host_maxfps` is also the FPS limit option in the video menu [2].

If you want uncapped rendering while still controlling your network update rate, use a negative value: `host_maxfps -100` renders as fast as your PC allows but sends 100 packets per second [1]. The code suggests a range of 10–150 pps, and `-40` matches a server's 0.025-second tick [1].

To cap your framerate at your monitor's refresh rate instead, enable vsync with `vid_vsync 1` (default `0`) [3]. Be aware that if your driver forces vsync off, this cvar has no effect and the engine will print a console message saying so [3].

To see your current FPS, set `scr_showfps 1` (default `0`) [4].

answers.question: The game is too dark. How do I adjust brightness and gamma?
answers.answer:
Type `gamma 0.8` in the console to brighten the screen — values below 1 are brighter, values above 1 are darker, and the default is `1` [1]. The setting is saved to your config [1].

If raising gamma looks washed out, try `contrast 1.2` instead: it gives less of a gray look, but colors near white get clipped to white [2]. Default is `1` [2].

- Mapshots (the level preview images) have their own brightness: `cl_mapshots_brightness`, default `0.8`; `1` keeps the compensated source brightness, lower values dim it [3].
- Gamma correction normally uses a GLSL path that fixes known issues like the screen staying dark after quitting [4]. You can force it with `-glslgamma` [5], or force hardware gamma ramps with `-hwgamma` if you have problems [6]. To disable the GLSL path, launch with `-noglslgamma` [4].

To inspect lighting itself, `r_lightmap 1` replaces textures with white so only lightmaps show; default `0` [7].

answers.question: How do I get the classic pixelated look, or smooth textures instead?
answers.answer:
Texture filtering is controlled by `gl_texturemode`, which defaults to `""` [1]. Type `gl_describetexturemodes` in the console to list every valid mode name [2].

- Pixelated, software-like look: `gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST` — point sampled, lowest quality, highest performance [1].
- Smoothest look: `gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` — trilinear, highest quality, lowest performance [1].
- No blending: `gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR` [1].
- Sharp pixels with better distant textures: `GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR` or `GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST` [1].

For sharper textures at oblique angles, raise `gl_texture_anisotropy` from its default `1` to `2`, `4`, `8`, or `16` [3].

For a chunky low-resolution look, `r_scale` renders the view at reduced resolution: `r_scale 2` is 1/2, `3` is 1/3, `4` is 1/4 [4]. Default is `1` [4].

answers.question: How do I hide or reposition the weapon model?
answers.answer:
Hide it with `r_drawviewmodel 0`; the default is `1`, and it's saved to your config [1]. Some players do this to see more of the screen and aim with the crosshair instead [1].

To move the weapon model rather than hide it, use the viewmodel offset variables:

- `cl_gunx` — positive moves it right; default `0`, clamped to -30 through 30 [2][3]
- `cl_guny` — positive moves it down; default `0` [3]
- `cl_gunz` — positive moves it forward; default `0` [3]

For the classic WinQuake gun position, set `r_viewmodel_quake 1` (default `0`) [4].

Note that `scr_ofsx` shifts the whole game screen sideways, not the weapon, and isn't saved to your config [5].

answers.question: How do I change my crosshair's style, color, and size?
answers.answer:
Turn the crosshair on with `crosshair 1` (default is `0`, off). Values up to 7 give different styles [1].

To recolor it, set `scr_crosshaircolor` — it accepts hex RGB or Quake colors 1–13, default `0xffffff` (white) [2]. For example `scr_crosshaircolor 0x00ff00` for green.

To resize it, use `scr_crosshairscale`: `1` is normal, `10` is maximum enlargement (default `1`) [3].

Other useful settings:

- `scr_crosshairalpha` — crosshair opacity, default `1` [4].
- `scr_crosshaircshift` — color the crosshair shifts to when you take damage, default `0xfc7303` [5].
- `cl_damagehuecolor` — sets the damage hue color, default `0xeb580e` [6].
- `cl_menucrosshair 1` — keeps the crosshair visible while a menu is open (default `0`) [7].

All of these save to your config [2][4][3].

answers.question: How do I change the HUD style and size?
answers.answer:
Change HUD style with `scr_sbar`: default `1`, `2` for QW style, `3` for QE [1].

Change HUD size with `scr_sbarscale`: default `1`; `2` doubles the statusbar. Integer values look nicest, and it never draws smaller than 1:1 or wider than the window [2].

To change how much screen the HUD takes up, use `viewsize` (default `100`) or `sizeup`/`sizedown`, which change it in steps of 10 from 30 to 120 [3][4][5]. At `viewsize 110` the weapon status bar disappears; at `120` the health status bar disappears [5].

For HUD transparency, use `scr_sbaralpha`: default `0.75`, `0` is invisible, `1` is opaque [6].

answers.question: How do I show my FPS, ping, and a clock on screen?
answers.answer:
Type these in the console (open it with the `~` key):

- `scr_showfps 1` — shows FPS, default `0` [1]
- `scr_ping 1` — shows ping in the lower-left; this is already the default `1`, and packet loss appears only when drops occur [2]
- `scr_clock 2` — 12-hour system clock in the lower-right; default `0` [3]

For the clock you can pick a different style instead of `2`: `1` level time (MM:SS), `3` 24-hour clock, `4` date only, `5`/`6` date plus time, `7`/`8` dynamic date-or-time depending on whether scores are visible [3].

Example for a clock showing date and time: `scr_clock 6` [3].

Since the FPS and clock settings are saved to your config, they'll stick between sessions [1][3].

answers.question: How do I open the console and change its size or font scale?
answers.answer:
Open it with the `toggleconsole` command, which lowers or raises the console screen [1]. The key it's bound to by default isn't covered here, so check your key bindings in-game.

To resize it:

- `scr_consize` sets the console's vertical length while the game is active; default is `.5` (half the screen) [2].
- `scr_conscale` scales the console text larger, but only takes effect when `scr_conwidth` is 0; default `1` [3].
- `scr_conwidth` sets the virtual console width, where smaller numbers mean larger text; default `0` uses the window width. Values below 320 or above the window width are clamped, and values are rounded to a multiple of 8 [4].
- `scr_autoscale` is a command that automatically calculates a UI scale from your current resolution and applies it to the console, menus, status bar, and crosshair [5].

For a bigger scrollback buffer, launch with `-consize` (in kilobytes); the default is 65536, and 16k is the minimum [6].

answers.question: How do I adjust mouse sensitivity and turn off mouse acceleration?
answers.answer:
Use `sensitivity` for overall mouse speed — default is `3` [1]. Most players tune it so a wrist flick turns you about 180 degrees; try `seta sensitivity 5` and adjust from there [1][2]. Use `seta` (not `set`) so the value is saved to your config and persists across restarts [2].

For vertical look, `m_pitch` defaults to `0.022`; set it to `-0.022` for inverted (airplane-style) pitch [3]. Leave it at ±0.022 and change `sensitivity` instead for overall feel [3].

Mouse acceleration: on macOS, `in_disablemacosxmouseaccel` defaults to `2`, which disables system acceleration so it doesn't affect game sensitivity [4]. Values of `1` request the legacy disable path [5]. The available data doesn't cover disabling acceleration on Windows or Linux.

If aim still feels wrong, run `in_mouseinfo` to print your current mouse input configuration and diagnostics [6].

answers.question: How do I bind keys and make aliases?
answers.answer:
Use `bind` to attach commands to keys, and `alias` to create named command shortcuts. For one command: `bind <key> <command>`. For multiple commands, quote them and separate with semicolons: `bind <key> "cmd1; cmd2"` [1]. Non-printing keys use their key name; Escape and `~` can only be bound from an external config file [1]. Remove one with `unbind <key>` [2]; list all with `bindlist` [3].

Create an alias with `alias "name" "value"` [4]. Typing `alias` alone prints all aliases and assignments [5]; `aliaslist` gives an alphabetized list, optionally filtered by substring [6]. `unaliasall` deletes all aliases [7].

By default `cfg_save_aliases` is `1`, so non-server aliases are saved to config.cfg [8], and `cfg_unbindall` is `1`, so stored bindings load after an unbindall [9]. `cl_aliasoverlap` defaults to `1`, letting aliases override cvars; if set to `0`, a conflicting alias is renamed with `_a` [10].

answers.question: How do I turn on mouse look and always run?
answers.answer:
Type `+mlook` in the console to turn mouse look on, and `-mlook` to turn it off [1][2]. While mouse look is active, moving the mouse forward/back looks up/down instead of moving you, so `m_forward` has no effect [3].

For always run, type `cl_alwaysrun 1`. It defaults to `0` [4]. With it on, you run without holding a key, and the run key instead acts as a walk/slow key [4]. Note this is the Quakespasm behavior, which differs slightly from vanilla's always-run movement speeds [4].

answers.question: Can I play with a gamepad or controller?
answers.answer:
Yes. Controller support is enabled by default: `joy_enable` defaults to `1` [1]. Set `joy_enable 0` to turn it off entirely [1].

- Look speed: `joy_sensitivity_yaw` (default `240`) and `joy_sensitivity_pitch` (default `130`) set the maximum turning speed in degrees per second [2][3].
- If your pad is detected but buttons are wrong, run `gamecontrollerdb_reload` to reload SDL controller mappings and reopen the current controller [4].
- Button names shown in the bindings menu adapt to the connected pad type (Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo) [5].

The available settings don't stop there: deadzones, inversion, rumble, flick turning, touchpad and gyro options also exist as console variables [3]. QSS-M does not document a dedicated controller menu in the material here, so configure these through the console.

answers.question: How do I connect to a multiplayer server?
answers.answer:
Use the `connect` command with the server's IP address, DNS hostname, or local network name [1]. The default port is 26000; if the server uses a different port, set `port` to that number first [1].

- To find servers on your local network, run `slist`, then `connect` using a name from the list [2].
- If you get dropped or your connection fails, run `reconnect` to rejoin the last server without retyping the address [3].
- `net_connectattempts` controls how many connection retries are made (default `3`) [4].
- `net_connecttimeout` sets how many seconds a stalled handshake waits before aborting (default `10`) [5].
- `net_connectsearch` (default `1`) makes `connect` do a local host search before connecting; set it to `0` to skip that and go straight to the address [6].

To leave a server, use `disconnect` [7].

answers.question: How do I set my player name and colors?
answers.answer:
Type `name YourName` in the console to set your player name — QSS-M lets you edit it by just typing `name`, which is handy for names with special characters [1]. The `name` cvar defaults to `"player"` and is saved to your config [2].

For colors, use the `color` command [3]:

- `color` alone reports your current shirt and pants colors.
- `color 4` sets both shirt and pants to the same color.
- `color 4 13` sets shirt and pants separately.
- `color x x` gives you random colors.

Valid colors run from 0 to 13; anything above that just makes you look blue [3]. Typing `color` with no arguments also prints the full list, from 0 (white) through 13 (blue) [4].

answers.question: How can I reduce lag or make online play feel smoother?
answers.answer:
There's no single "reduce lag" switch here, but a few settings affect how smooth online play feels.

- `pq_lag` adds artificial lag, it doesn't remove it. It takes 0–400 ms and defaults to `0` [1]. Leave it at `0` unless you're deliberately simulating a bad connection; the notes also mention a `ping +X` form [1].
- `cl_nolerp` defaults to `0`, which keeps entity movement interpolated and smooth. Setting it to `1` stops predicting entity movement, so objects jump from point to point instead [2].
- `cl_nopred` also defaults to `0` [3]; it's the prediction toggle, so leaving it off is the normal choice.

For movement feel rather than network lag, `sv_accelerate` (default `10`) and the pmove-only `sv_airaccelerate`/`sv_wateraccelerate` are server-side [4][5][6]. Nothing here covers general ping reduction.

answers.question: How do I chat, team chat, and mute other players?
answers.answer:
Chat to everyone with `messagemode` (type, Enter sends, Esc cancels) [1], or type/bind `say <message>` [2]. Team chat uses `messagemode2` [3] or `say_team <message>` [4]; `messagemode2` is not bound by default [3].

- Text chat mute: `ignore <name>` hides that player’s chat; `ignore` alone lists ignored players; `unignore <name>` restores them. Partial names work, and the list clears when you disconnect [5][6].
- Voice chat mute: `vignore <slot> 1` mutes that client slot, `vignore <slot> 0` unmutes, and `unmuteall` clears all voice ignores [7][8].
- `mute` toggles sound volume (CTRL-M also works); it is not a per-player mute [9].

`cl_chatmode` defaults to `0`; set `cl_chatmode 1` to send anything Quake can’t interpret as chat, so you can type without `say` [10][11].

answers.question: How do I host my own server?
answers.answer:
Start the engine with a server launch option, then set a few variables.

- Dedicated server: launch with `-dedicated` (defaults to 16 players; max is 16) [1]. A listen server (you also play) uses `-listen 16` [2]. Listen servers aren't recommended as public servers [2].
- Name it: `hostname "My Server"` — default is `UNNAMED` [3].
- Pick a mode: `deathmatch 3` is recommended for a public server; `1` is common for one-on-one [4]. Default is `0` [4].
- Player count: `maxplayers` sets the maximum. A listen server starts at 4, a dedicated one at 8, and 16 requires `-listen 16` or `-dedicated 16` [2].
- Port: the default is 26000; override with `-port <n>` (or `-udpport`) [5][6].

The dedicated server stays in text mode, with most console commands still available [1].

answers.question: How do I record and play back demos?
answers.answer:
To record, type `record` with no arguments; QSS-M saves the demo to `id1/demos` using the map name and date as the filename [1]. Stop recording with `stop`, which writes the demo to disk [2]. The format is set by `cl_demo_format`, default `dem`; supported builds also accept `dz` for compressed DZip archives [3]. For automatic recording, use `cl_autodemo`, default `0` (off); values `1`–`4` control when it records [4].

To play back, use `playdemo <name>` [5]. Stop playback with `stopdemo` [6]. For a playlist, use `startdemos demo1 demo2 ...` (up to 32 demos, no `.dem` extension needed), then `demos` [7][8]. This requires `cl_demoreel` enabled; it defaults to `1` [9][7].

answers.question: How do I take screenshots, and where are they saved?
answers.answer:
Type `screenshot` in the console to capture the current frame. It accepts optional format and quality arguments: `screenshot png 100`, or `tga`/`jpg` with a quality of 1–100 [1][2]. Without arguments it uses the default format.

Screenshots are written to the game directory — the same place savegames, demos and config files go. That directory can be overridden at launch with the `-game` command line parameter [3]. The engine does not change it while running.

If you'd rather not have your player name appear in the image, set `cl_contentfilter 1`, which hides IPs in the multiplayer menu and user name prints for condump and screenshots [4].

You can also bind a key to a screenshot sequence; the example binds use `screenshot jpg 100` [1].

answers.question: How do I change volume and music?
answers.answer:
Type `volume 0.5` to set overall sound and music loudness — the default is `0.7` [1]. Background CD music has its own control: `bgmvolume 0.5` (default `1`) [2]. Ambient sounds like wind and water use `ambient_level` (default `0.3`) [3].

For external music files, put them in `Quake/id1/music` named like `track02.ogg` (there is no track01) [4]. Playback of these files is on by default via `bgm_extmusic 1`; set it to `0` to disable, or launch with `-noextmusic` [5][6]. Supported formats include MP3, OGG, FLAC, WAV, and tracker modules [4][7].

Useful commands: `music <name>` to play a track (no extension needed), `music_stop`, `music_pause`, `music_resume`, `music_loop`, and `music_jump` for module music [4][8][9][10][11][12]. `music_preview` plays a file without replacing gameplay music [13].

answers.question: QSS-M won't start or crashes. What should I try?
answers.answer:
The available settings cover a few common culprits, but general crash troubleshooting isn't documented here.

- Rule out sound: launch with `-nosound` to disable hardware sound [1]. In-game you can instead set `nosound 1`, though it won't fully silence everything until you restart or change maps [2]. If you changed audio settings, `snd_restart` reinitializes sound [3].
- Capture a log: launch with `-condebug` to write the console to `qconsole.log` [4]. You can cap it, e.g. `-condebug 5` for 5 MiB; no number means unlimited [5]. In-game, `condump` writes the console buffer to `condump.txt` [6].
- Video mode problems: after changing `vid_width`, `vid_height`, `vid_fullscreen`, `vid_bpp`, or `vid_refreshrate`, run `vid_restart` to apply them [7]. Note `vid_bpp` defaults to 16 and is ignored in windowed mode [8].

If none of these help, the cause isn't covered by the documented options.

answers.question: Why does the game stutter or the sound crackle?
answers.answer:
Sound crackling is usually the sound buffer running dry when your framerate dips. `_snd_mixahead` controls how far ahead the engine mixes audio; at the default `0.1` seconds, anything below 10 fps runs off the end of the buffer and you get stuttering sound [1].

- Raise it: `_snd_mixahead 0.2` handles framerates as low as 5 fps [1].
- Be reasonable: a larger mixahead makes the CPU mix more sound each frame, which can lower your framerate and defeat the point [1].

If the stutter is general rather than audio-only, check your frame cap. `host_maxfps` defaults to `250`, and `0` uncaps it [2]; `vid_vsync` defaults to `0`, so vsync isn't limiting you unless you set it to `1` [3].

For a sound stuck in an endless loop, `stopsound` halts all playback [4].

answers.question: How do I find a setting when I don't know its name?
answers.answer:
Type `apropos <text>` or `find <text>` in the console. Both search command and console-variable names for the substring you give, so you can search by a word you remember [1][2].

For example, if you know part of the name, try `apropos fov` or `find fov`.

You can also list everything alphabetically:

- `cmdlist` lists all commands; add a substring to list only commands starting with it [3].
- `cvarlist` lists all console variables; add a substring to list only cvars starting with it [4].

So use `apropos`/`find` when you only know a concept, and `cmdlist`/`cvarlist` when you know the start of the name.
